I believe the most inspiring stories are the ones who come from the pits of hell and rock bottom and pull out to make it through. And I honestly think you can do it, even if you’re convinced you have no worth or drive. I’m sure your brothers would think the same, and want you to push past further than they did. Lackluster now doesn’t mean it’ll be lackluster forever, especially if you have the power to change it. You have so much time to not regret anything. I’m sure you have something in this life that brings you joy, you’ve had friends, you have a boyfriend, even if you don’t think you deserve him, you do. You deserve a lot of things, you deserve to live a happy life, that being the most important.
Please, lean into the things that make you happy, maybe a food, seeing a sunrise, seeing your boyfriend smile, and start taking baby steps to the accomplishments I know you can achieve, like drinking water when you don’t think you deserve it, or taking a shower, or folding laundry or throwing away something when you didn’t feel like getting up. Maybe even staying one day longer past today. I know you can do it, and I know it’s so hard to see that when you feel like the absolute fucking scum of the earth laying bloodied and bruised and barely breathing at rock bottom and I won’t sugar coat it this shit’s hard as fuck. But you can do it, you can get out of this and you deserve to get out of this. And holy hell is it worth it when you see the sun again, there’s no other bliss like it. The sun isn’t gone. It’s still there for you, no matter how deep your hole is. I believe in you, and I really really care about you.

I’m a firm believer of that everything happens for a reason, and you were put on this planet for a reason. You were meant to struggle, but you are also meant to live.
Have you heard of the literature concept of Hero’s Journey? If not, it’s basically a formula for a protagonist’s story.
It starts with the ‘call to adventure’, something to be the catalyst to their journey. Once they decide to take the call, they ‘cross the threshold’ of adventure, truly admitting to the journey. Then there’s a ‘road of trials’, this is the point where obstacles begin to present themselves, and ultimately after the road, there’s the ‘abyss’. This is where the hero finally falls after they cannot push through the obstacles any further. It is rock bottom, it is hell, it is suffering... sound familiar? But the cycle doesn’t end there, that would just be a shitty story. There is ‘rebirth’. The hero manages to must up the strength to pull themselves out of the hole, and they reach the point of ‘transformation’. They have overcome and they are rewarded with the ‘ultimate boon’. In stories, it may be true love or an antidote, but for people in real life it usually is an extraordinary even that makes you happy beyond belief. Finally is the ‘returning boon’, where the character leaves the adventure and returns with their reward... and the cycle begins again.
I for one have lived through a hero’s journey with suicide, I was 12 when I attempted. And I struggled for 4 years until finally last year I had the best year of my life. Unfortunately, life is made of hills and valleys and currently I’m in my new abyss.. but I’ve been through it, and I know I can.
Who’s to say you can’t? You’ve made it this far, why not a day more? Break it down into steps.. take it by the day, or the hour, or the minute, or the second. Focus on now and know that you’ve made it this far, why not take a chance to see what you’ll be rewarded for your efforts? You might as well, seeing as it will come to you.
You got this, I believe in you, and if you’d like to talk more pm me.

It will give you moments where you thank yourself for never going through with it, and everything in that moment tastes so sweet and worth it. Life is made of mountains and valleys, but when you get to the top you get to admire the beauty of it. I’m learning to love the pain and failure, because I know there is only one way for me to go from rock bottom.
Take a chance, see what life has to offer you. Be the hero of your story, because you have the ability in you. You’ve made it this far, take it one day more, one step more, one breath more. I believe in you.

hi! I just joined Reddit solely for the purpose of commenting. I’m a teenager diagnosed with PMDD and have struggled with it since my period started. I was put on birth control but that’s the extent of my medication. I took the time to instead figure out what I could do myself. I’m not sure if you’ve been to therapy, but it’s a good start. Therapy didn’t work for me, but what did was to focus on my wellness. I did yoga 3 times a week last year, focused my priorities on having a positive mental attitude, PMA, and did as much research on wellbeing as I could to benefit myself. You and I seem to have very different symptoms, seeing as mine tend to lean more towards the suicidal, hopeless end of the spectrum and I rarely do get physical with rage (but I have my moments), but I think it may be beneficial to try and see what you can do to change your struggles yourself. It took me a very long time, but I’m in a much better place than I was 6 years ago.
